description: This project explores the innovative integration of space imagery, sound, and colour through an interactive web experience. Users can upload NASA images and transform them into unique audiovisual experiences, where each image inspires distinctive soundscapes and colour palettes. By combining visual exploration with sound synthesis, the project offers a creative and engaging way to experience the beauty of space through a new sensory perspective.
summary:
SONORA is an innovative and interactive website that transforms images into sound through a process called image sonification. It combines science, technology, and creativity to provide users with a new way to experience visual information through audio.

The website features a NASA Image Library, where users can search for and select space photographs of planets, galaxies, stars, and Earth. Once an image is selected, SONORA analyses its colours, brightness, and texture, displaying the image's visual characteristics and colour palette.

Based on these visual features, the website generates soundscapes and melodies, allowing users to explore the connection between images and sound. Users can also adjust the volume, bass, echo, and reverb to customise their listening experience. An animated sound visualizer provides visual feedback while the audio plays.

SONORA is developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with the NASA Images API for image searching and the Web Audio API for sound generation. Its main purpose is to demonstrate how visual information can be transformed into an alternative sensory experience.

In conclusion, SONORA offers a creative way to explore images beyond sight by connecting visual analysis with sound. It encourages users to discover the relationship between science, technology, and music through an interactive digital platform.
details:
SONORA is an innovative and interactive website that transforms images into sound through a process known as image sonification. The project combines science, technology, and creativity to provide users with a new way to experience visual information through audio.

One of the main features of SONORA is the NASA Image Library, which allows users to search for and select space photographs. Users can explore images of galaxies, planets, stars, and Earth before transferring their chosen image into the Image Lab for analysis.

The website analyses visual characteristics such as colours, brightness, and texture. It displays a colour palette and information about the image, which can be used to influence musical elements such as pitch, rhythm, and tone. These features help transform visual information into a unique soundscape.

SONORA also includes audio controls that allow users to adjust volume, bass, echo, and reverb. An animated sound visualizer provides visual feedback while the sound is playing, making the experience more engaging and interactive.

The website is developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It uses the NASA Images API to search for space photographs, HTML Canvas to analyse image pixels, and the Web Audio API to generate sound and apply audio effects.

The main objective of this project is to demonstrate how images can be experienced beyond sight. It encourages creativity, supports learning, and introduces users to the connection between visual information and sound. In the future, SONORA could be improved with more varied melodies, more accurate colour analysis, and options to save generated soundscapes.

In conclusion, SONORA brings image analysis and sound generation together in one creative platform, offering a new way to explore and experience images.
